title: Base rates
description: A good detector can still raise mostly false alarms.
question: If a part is flagged, how likely is it actually defective?

probability.posterior.label: Defect given a flag
probability.posterior.description: P(D | +): probability of a defect among flagged parts, undefined if no part can be flagged.

assumptions: p is the defect rate; sensitivity is P(+ | D); the false positive rate is P(+ | not D).
Counts are expectations, not outcomes from a random sample.
Every part is classified as flagged or unflagged.
limitations: This factory example does not model dependence between repeated tests.
Expected counts can be fractional; display rounding does not alter calculations.
Conditional probability is undefined when the flagged event has probability zero.

sources.title: OpenStax Principles of Data Science · 3.4 Probability Theory

review.scope: Technical reference checks only. Independent subject review and learner evaluation have not been completed.

concept: The base rate changes the balance of true and false positives in the flagged population.
misconception: P(defective | flagged) equals the sensitivity P(flagged | defective).
